{"question":"NEP 50에서 Python의 int·float·complex는 어떤 방식으로 타입을 취급하고, 값은 승격과 새 타입 변환에서 각각 어떻게 쓰여? NEP 51이 바꾸려는 스칼라 표현은 무엇이며 일반 print 출력과 배열 표현도 변경 범위에 들어가?","response_language":"ko","sources":[{"title":"NEP 50 - Promotion rules for Python scalars — Proposed weak promotion","meeting_date":null,"spans":[{"id":0,"text":"Proposed weak promotion
"},{"id":1,"text":"-----------------------
"},{"id":2,"text":"
"},{"id":3,"text":"This proposal uses a "weak scalar" logic.  This means that Python ``int``, ``float``,
"},{"id":4,"text":"and ``complex`` are not assigned one of the typical dtypes, such as float64 or int64.
"},{"id":5,"text":"Rather, they are assigned a special abstract DType, similar to the "scalar" hierarchy
"},{"id":6,"text":"names: Integral, Floating, ComplexFloating.
"},{"id":7,"text":"
"},{"id":8,"text":"When promotion occurs (as it does for ufuncs if no exact loop matches),
"},{"id":9,"text":"the other DType is able to decide how to regard the Python
"},{"id":10,"text":"scalar.  E.g. a ``UInt16`` promoting with an ``Integral`` will give ``UInt16``.
"},{"id":11,"text":"
"},{"id":12,"text":".. note::
"},{"id":13,"text":"
"},{"id":14,"text":"    A default will most likely be provided in the future for user-defined DTypes.
"},{"id":15,"text":"    Most likely this will end up being the default integer/float, but in principle
"},{"id":16,"text":"    more complex schemes could be implemented.
"},{"id":17,"text":"
"},{"id":18,"text":"At no time is the value used to decide the result of this promotion.  The value is only
"},{"id":19,"text":"considered when it is converted to the new dtype; this may raise an error.
"},{"id":20,"text":"
"},{"id":21,"text":"
"}]},{"title":"NEP 51 - Changing the representation of NumPy scalars — Motivation and scope","meeting_date":null,"spans":[{"id":22,"text":"Motivation and scope
"},{"id":23,"text":"====================
"},{"id":24,"text":"
"},{"id":25,"text":"This NEP proposes to change the representation of the following
"},{"id":26,"text":"NumPy scalars types to distinguish them from the Python scalars:
"},{"id":27,"text":"
"},{"id":28,"text":"* ``np.bool_``
"},{"id":29,"text":"* ``np.uint8``, ``np.int8``, and all other integer scalars
"},{"id":30,"text":"* ``np.float16``, ``np.float32``, ``np.float64``, ``np.longdouble``
"},{"id":31,"text":"* ``np.complex64``, ``np.complex128``, ``np.clongdouble``
"},{"id":32,"text":"* ``np.str_``, ``np.bytes_``
"},{"id":33,"text":"* ``np.void``  (structured dtypes)
"},{"id":34,"text":"
"},{"id":35,"text":"Additionally, the representation of the remaining NumPy scalars will be
"},{"id":36,"text":"adapted to print as ``np.`` rather than ``numpy.``:
"},{"id":37,"text":"
"},{"id":38,"text":"* ``np.datetime64`` and ``np.timedelta64``
"},{"id":39,"text":"* ``np.void``  (unstructured version)
"},{"id":40,"text":"
"},{"id":41,"text":"The NEP does not propose to change how these scalars print – only
"},{"id":42,"text":"their representation (``__repr__``) will be changed.
"},{"id":43,"text":"Further, array representation will not be affected since it already
"},{"id":44,"text":"includes the ``dtype=`` when necessary.
"},{"id":45,"text":"
"},{"id":46,"text":"The main motivation behind the change is that the Python numerical types
"},{"id":47,"text":"behave differently from the NumPy scalars.
"},{"id":48,"text":"For example numbers with lower precision (e.g. ``uint8`` or ``float16``)
"},{"id":49,"text":"should be used with care and users should be aware when they are working
"},{"id":50,"text":"with them.  All NumPy integers can experience overflow which Python integers
"},{"id":51,"text":"do not.
"},{"id":52,"text":"These differences will be exacerbated when adopting :ref:`NEP 50 <NEP50>`
"},{"id":53,"text":"because the lower precision NumPy scalar will be preserved more often.
"},{"id":54,"text":"Even ``np.float64``, which is very similar to Python's ``float`` and inherits
"},{"id":55,"text":"from it, does behave differently for example when dividing by zero.
"},{"id":56,"text":"
"},{"id":57,"text":"Another common source of confusion are the NumPy booleans.  Python programmers
"},{"id":58,"text":"sometimes write ``obj is True`` and will surprised when an object that shows
"},{"id":59,"text":"as ``True`` fails to pass the test.
"},{"id":60,"text":"It is much easier to understand this behavior when the value is
"},{"id":61,"text":"shown as ``np.True_``.
"},{"id":62,"text":"
"},{"id":63,"text":"Not only do we expect the change to help users better understand and be
"},{"id":64,"text":"reminded of the differences between NumPy and Python scalars, but we also
"},{"id":65,"text":"believe that the awareness will greatly help debugging.
"},{"id":66,"text":"
"}]}]}

"},{"id":24,"text":"    >>> np.float32(3.0)
"},{"id":25,"text":"    np.float32(3.0)
"},{"id":26,"text":"
"},{"id":27,"text":"We expect that this change will help users distinguish the NumPy scalars
"},{"id":28,"text":"from the Python builtin types and clarify their behavior.
"},{"id":29,"text":"
"},{"id":30,"text":"The distinction between NumPy scalars and Python builtins will further become
"},{"id":31,"text":"more important for users once :ref:`NEP 50 <NEP50>` is adopted.
"},{"id":32,"text":"
"},{"id":33,"text":"These changes do lead to smaller incompatible and infrastructure changes
"},{"id":34,"text":"related to array printing.
"},{"id":35,"text":"
"}]},{"title":"NEP 51 - Changing the representation of NumPy scalars — Backward compatibility","meeting_date":null,"spans":[{"id":36,"text":"Backward compatibility
"},{"id":37,"text":"======================
"},{"id":38,"text":"
"},{"id":39,"text":"We expect that most workflows will not be affected as only printing
"},{"id":40,"text":"changes.  In general we believe that informing users about the type
"},{"id":41,"text":"they are working with outweighs the need for adapting printing in
"},{"id":42,"text":"some instances.
"},{"id":43,"text":"
"},{"id":44,"text":"The NumPy test suite includes code such as ``decimal.Decimal(repr(scalar))``.
"},{"id":45,"text":"This code needs to be modified to use the ``str()``.
"},{"id":46,"text":"
"},{"id":47,"text":"An exception to this are downstream libraries with documentation and
"},{"id":48,"text":"especially documentation testing.
"},{"id":49,"text":"Since the representation of many values will change, in many cases
"},{"id":50,"text":"the documentation will have to be updated.
"},{"id":51,"text":"This is expected to require larger documentation fixups in the mid-term.
"},{"id":52,"text":"
"},{"id":53,"text":"It may be necessary to adopt tools for doctest testing to
"},{"id":54,"text":"allow approximate value checking for the new representation.
"},{"id":55,"text":"
"}]},{"title":"NEP 50 - Promotion rules for Python scalars — Proposed weak promotion","meeting_date":null,"spans":[{"id":56,"text":"Proposed weak promotion
"},{"id":57,"text":"-----------------------
"},{"id":58,"text":"
"},{"id":59,"text":"This proposal uses a "weak scalar" logic.  This means that Python ``int``, ``float``,
"},{"id":60,"text":"and ``complex`` are not assigned one of the typical dtypes, such as float64 or int64.
"},{"id":61,"text":"Rather, they are assigned a special abstract DType, similar to the "scalar" hierarchy
"},{"id":62,"text":"names: Integral, Floating, ComplexFloating.
"},{"id":63,"text":"
"},{"id":64,"text":"When promotion occurs (as it does for ufuncs if no exact loop matches),
"},{"id":65,"text":"the other DType is able to decide how to regard the Python
"},{"id":66,"text":"scalar.  E.g. a ``UInt16`` promoting with an ``Integral`` will give ``UInt16``.
"},{"id":67,"text":"
"},{"id":68,"text":".. note::
"},{"id":69,"text":"
"},{"id":70,"text":"    A default will most likely be provided in the future for user-defined DTypes.
"},{"id":71,"text":"    Most likely this will end up being the default integer/float, but in principle
"},{"id":72,"text":"    more complex schemes could be implemented.
"},{"id":73,"text":"
"},{"id":74,"text":"At no time is the value used to decide the result of this promotion.  The value is only
"},{"id":75,"text":"considered when it is converted to the new dtype; this may raise an error.
"},{"id":76,"text":"
"},{"id":77,"text":"
"}]}]}
